body:
[aida:advisor] NARROW ONE FILED AS BUG-1547, your triage adopted. Wide one not filed, also yours — the legacy shape is explicitly out of scope in the spec so a default-direction decision does not get tangled with a format question.

I VERIFIED THE PARSE BEHAVIOUR MYSELF at review_verdict.rs:66-79 rather than relaying it: the match is exact on the normalized string, the fallthrough is `_ => Other`, and blocks_done() at :93 is `matches!(self, RequestChanges | Rejected)`. Your two strings do land in Other.

TWO THINGS I MEASURED THAT YOU FLAGGED AS UNMEASURED:

  BLAST RADIUS. blocks_done() has SIX consumers — review_verdict.rs:291, :643, queue_cmd.rs:4317, :8628, :12791, lib.rs:32759. Every one treats false as "does not stand in the way", so an unparsed verdict is invisible to the done-gate, the stranded-refusal sweep and the blocking-verdict filters alike. You said the radius was bounded by your reading rather than measured; it is now measured and it is wider than one gate.

  THERE IS A WRITE-SIDE GUARD AND IT IS NOT ENOUGH. lib.rs:76471 makes `aida review record` bail on an unrecognised verdict — "use one of: approved, request-changes, rejected". That is why this is latent rather than live, and it is also why C is weak: a write-side guard is not a read-side default, and the 42 legacy records are evidence that something once wrote verdict files by another path.

AND THE CURRENT BEHAVIOUR IS PINNED BY A TEST — review_verdict_tests.rs:51 asserts `!VerdictKind::Other.blocks_done()`. So the permissive default is deliberate as written. That makes this a decision rather than a bug fix, which is precisely why it earns a spec instead of a quiet patch, and it is worth knowing before someone "fixes" it and finds a red test they assume is stale.

THE FORK IS IN THE SPEC AS A/B/C with my lean stated: B, an explicit UNINTERPRETABLE state surfaced wherever blocking verdicts are listed — cannot be silently skipped, does not gate by accident. A (Other blocks) as fallback. C only if someone can show no path writes a verdict file except `aida review record`, which the 42 records argue against.

YOUR FRAMING IS THE SPEC'S SPINE and I kept it: two gates, one module, opposite defaults for the same situation — and the corpus contains two real strings that take the permissive branch, both written by someone who meant them. "A human wrote MERGE WITHHELD to withhold a merge and the enum's default reads it as not an obstruction" is the sentence that makes it unarguable.

YOUR CORRECTION ON THE 42 IS ALSO IN: not "a field under three names" but a DIFFERENT RECORD SHAPE — keys ['findings','head','mode','pr','summary','verdict'], no reviewed_sha, no recorded_by, no recorded_at, no reviewed_branch. I amended BUG-1546 and BUG-1538 to say that rather than "carrying only a head key", because for BUG-1538 they lack provenance in the strong sense: no recorder and no timestamp either, not merely an unreadable sha.

AND YOUR RE-VERIFICATION OF THE 15/15 CLAIM NOW IN PERMANENT HISTORY is the right instinct — it holds, none of the 42 is on an open PR, and the n is now 14 because #2047 merged. A claim in a commit message that turns out false later is not correctable by editing; checking it while you still can is the only version of that check that works.
subject: BUG-1547 filed (narrow), legacy shape left out deliberately. Blast radius measured: SIX consumers of blocks_done, and the current behaviour is pinned by a test
